Messages.Author: Malone
Messages.Body:
The announcement of the upcoming Rebellion expansion may mean that
this question has already been settled, for the time being... but
anyway...

A discussion a few weeks ago about Anarchs included, among other
things, a little bit of debate about out-of-the-box Anarchs. The two
sides are basically "Just go ahead and print them, already" and
"Anarch is distinct from other traits because of how it is acquired,
let's maintain that distinctness".

Things usually not being exactly black-and-white, there's some middle
ground here. One option proposed was (a small number of) vampires
that, per special text, could go Anarch by burning some blood or pool
and/or tapping during some appropriate window. Another was (a small
number of) 4-cap Anarchs, possibly one standard-disciplined 4-cap from
each clan, that ignored the grouping requirements.

It seems like vampires that ignore the grouping rules (I'll call them
group 0) are a design possibility that will eventually be exploited,
if the game lives long enough. Putting user-friendly Anarchs there
would be a mistake, though, at least if you believe maintaining
distinct mechanisms for distinct traits is desireable. It would
change the Anarch trait from one that requires effort to acquire into
the most readily available in the game. (Imagine a bunch of group 0
Seraphs, one from each clan, or Princes, or...) And from the
standpoint of needing to keep printing and selling new cards, a bunch
of group 0 Anarchs would be a one-shot, unrepeatable thing that would
also weigh against the later release of grouped ootb Anarchs.

Here's another angle for having ootb Anarchs that wouldn't genericize
the trait too much (in my opinion, which is grounded in trying to
respect the trait's distinctness).

Alice, Thin-blood Anarch
Caitiff, capacity 2, group 2
Independent, Anarch. Thin-blood Anarchs are not unique. When this
Alice enters play, choose a discipline; this Alice may play cards
requiring an Anarch as though she had that discipline at the basic
level. During your untap phase, burn 2 pool if you do not control an
older, ready, unique Anarch.

Bill, Thin-blood Anarch
Caitiff, capacity 2, group 4
Independent, Anarch. Thin-blood Anarchs are not unique. When Bill
enters play you may search you hand, library or ash heap for a Master:
Discipline card and place it on him. During your untap phase, burn 2
pool if you do not control an older, ready, unique Anarch.

Cathy, Thin-blood Anarch
Caitiff, capacity 2, group 6
Independent, Anarch. Thin-blood Anarchs are not unique. Once per
turn, Alice may play a card requiring an Anarch as though she had any
one discipline at the basic level. During your untap phase, burn 2
pool if you do not control an older, ready, unique Anarch.

etc.

See, but it is a bad comparison. There is nothing that a (Prince or
Seraph) mechanic needs to fix them. The Anarch mechanic arguably needs
a fixing. Adding a handful of "Group Zero" or whatever pre existing
anarchs fixes a problem with the anarch mechanic (that it is too
costly to go anarch currently)--you have someone who can play cards
out of the gate, and it makes going anarch the hard way cheaper across
the board. Making them Group Zero (i.e. groupless) gives all group
pairs the ability to take advantage of this fix without adding
anything else significant to each group pair, assuming the Group Zero
pre packaged anarchs were fairly generic (i.e. 4 cap with 3 inclan
disciplines at inferior and inherrent anarch trait--are the Nosferatu
*really* going to benefit from getting a second Sammy?)

Adding "Group Zero" Princes or Seraphs increases the power of an
already effective group (i.e. Princes or Seraphs) by adding more of
the same to each group. It isn't a good example.

-Peter

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
In article
<0a421a57-d66f-4a34...@h11g2000prf.googlegroups.com>,

> Uhm, I've never played Anarchs (yet). Could someone explain why

To piggyback on what Fred wrote, those who see a problem with the "go
anarch" mechanic (which isn't everyone, mind you, but it isn't at all
unusual to see folks critisizing the mechanic) generally feel that
filling your deck with cards that don't do anything other than let you
play some other cards in your deck is just too disadvantageous in the
long run to be worth the effort.

For example, if you need all your vampires to be anarchs (as you have a
lot of anarch tech in your deck--say you are relying on making multiple
Barons to pass votes and let you protect your Baron titles), and you
need them early and often (assume you want 4 vampires in play, and you
want all of them anarchs as soon as possible), you have some options,
none of which are great:

A) Include enough cards to make your guys anarch that you draw them
early and often--say, 12-13 slots dedicated to Galaric's Legacy, Go
Anarch, Seattle Committee. That is about 15% of your deck filled with
cards that don't do anything other than make you an anarch. And once all
of your vampires are anarchs, they don't even do that. So then you add a
few Power Base: LA so that you can cycle them out of your deck for a
handy untap. So then, let's say, you have 12 "go anarch" cards and 3
PB:LA (17% of your deck). You have a pretty good chance of having a go
anarch card in your opening hand, but also have a pretty good chance of
not ever seeing a PB:LA, and have a pretty good chance of not drawing
enough go anarch cards early enough anyway.

B) Include no go anarch tech at all, and plan on going anarch the hard
way. Saves deck space, costs blood and actions. Not necessarily a good
trade off.

In situations where you don't *need* to be an anarch immediately (i.e.
your anarch angle is limited in the deck), then you can add a couple
Seattle Committees or a small handful of Go Anarch or something and not
worry about it. But if you need your vampires to be anarchs and need
them anarach as soon as possible, as being an anarch is the mechanism
that makes your deck go, the two current options aren't great and
provide significant disincentive to bother even trying.

Peter D Bakija

And just to add a little more concrete data to what Peter wrote, if
you put 3 PB:LA in your 90-card deck, on average, you'll draw the
first on card 23, which is probably about the same time that all your
vamps are anarch and you want to start ditching Become Anarch cards.

Also, I'm not sure how many cards Peter expects to cycle in a game,
nor what a "pretty good chance of never seeing a PB:LA" means to him,
but to me, I expect to cycle at least 30 cards in a game, and "pretty
good chance" means >50%. So I disagree with the "pretty good chance
of never seeing a PB:LA" if you put 3 of them in your 90 card deck.

Regardless of what English you use, the actual numbers are:
You'll draw at least 1 PB:LA by card 23 in 50% of your games.
You'll draw at least 1 PB:LA by card 38 in 80% of your games.
You'll draw at least 1 PB:LA by card 55 in 95% of your games.

So, yes, there will certainly be some games that you don't see a
PB:LA, but the chances of that are directly related to the number of
total cards you cycle.

Ira, defender of the anarch mechanic, advocate of creating additional
powerful 3-way cards.

I'm not seeing the huge implications, really. I mean, like, I'm not
totally sold even on my own idea. But what are the huge implications
of a group zero anarch guy? I mean, assuming they are fairly generic,
not spectacular vampires--my original idea was make a generic 4 cap
for every clan who starts as an anarch and is grop zero (or whatever).
It would add an extra vampire to every clan in every group, but a
singularly unspectacular one (a 4 cap with 3 in clan inferior
disciplines). You could make a whole crypt out of them, but that isn't
impacted by the group aspect (i.e. you could make a whole crypt out of
them if they were all G4 also), and said crypt isn't likely to be that
useful, due to the large discipline spread, even taking the crazy
anarch 3 ways into account.

What are the huge implications you are seeing here? I'm not saying
there aren't any, but I'm not seeing what they are.

-Peter

Just that people inevitably find uses for such a vampire other than their
original intent. So, for instance, if you make a group zero 4-cap with
inferior potence, this would be usable for all potence decks which could
conceivably make use of such a vampire, anarch or not. Maybe 'huge' was
an unforunate choice of words (you know we Usenet denizens always pump

lasting than the standard vampires that are now being designed, given
that grouping is here to stay.

Fred

one vampire who ignores grouping rules.

Otherwise, creative texts for ootb anarchs with disadvantages is the
way to go, IMO.
